parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module has one cohesive concern: each file is a single use case for the project/task feature. It still fails on duplication and on inconsistent use of the abstraction. (1) The ID-generation rule appears twice: CreateProjectUseCase.generateId() and CreateTaskUseCase.generateId() have the same `${prefix}_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}` logic, so the ID format has no single home. (2) The use cases change a Task in different ways. MarkTaskAsDoneUseCase calls the entity's own method, task.markAsDone(). AssignTaskUseCase instead rebuilds the whole Task with `new Task(...)`, copying every field by hand and swapping in the new assignee, which skips any checks the entity might apply. A smaller issue: CreateTaskUseCase hard-codes 'todo' as the starting status, so that rule sits in the use case instead of the entity.

violations.message: The private generateId() repeats the ID-format rule also defined in CreateProjectUseCase.generateId(), so ID generation has no single home. It also hard-codes the starting status 'todo' instead of leaving it to the Task entity.
The private generateId() repeats the same Date.now()/Math.random() ID rule as CreateTaskUseCase, so the ID format must be changed in two places.

Changes a Task by rebuilding it with `new Task(...)` and copying every field by hand, instead of calling an entity method the way MarkTaskAsDoneUseCase calls task.markAsDone(). This skips the entity's own behavior and is inconsistent with the other use cases.
